name: Wraith Meridian
geological_features: A surface of ancient regolith undisturbed for billions of years
A single equatorial ridge dividing the body into two hemispheres of different albedo
Micro-crater fields so dense the surface resembles sandblasted metal
specific_features: A narrow band along the equatorial ridge that reflects radar at frequencies inconsistent with natural rock
resources: Platinum group metals in surface regolith
Helium-3 implanted by solar wind over billions of years
description: Wraith Meridian is barely a world at all, a dwarf body orbiting in the outer reaches of its system where sunlight arrives as a memory rather than a force. Its surface is a grey-brown waste of ancient regolith, untouched by geological activity for so long that the only features are impact craters layered upon impact craters, the record of billions of years of bombardment. The equatorial ridge that divides its two hemispheres is the sole geological feature of note, a raised spine of rock that casts the only natural shadows on an otherwise featureless sphere.

The two hemispheres differ in albedo by a measurable degree, one side slightly darker than the other, suggesting different surface compositions or exposure histories. In the negligible gravity, dust kicked up by footsteps takes minutes to settle, creating slow-motion clouds that drift with the walker. There is no sound, no weather, no change. Wraith Meridian is the definition of desolation, a place where time has stopped bothering to pass.

The radar anomaly along the equatorial ridge was detected during routine survey and has resisted explanation. A narrow band, roughly two meters wide and running the full circumference of the body, reflects radar at frequencies that do not match the surrounding regolith or any known natural mineral. Ground-penetrating radar suggests the anomaly extends several meters below the surface. Excavation of a test section revealed a smooth, dark material of unknown composition that resisted sample extraction with standard tools.

Wraith Meridian has no strategic value beyond its platinum deposits and the equatorial anomaly. The former can be harvested by automated systems, and the latter has attracted a small research team that maintains a pressurized habitat on the darker hemisphere. Their progress on the anomaly material has been slow, as it resists every analytical technique applied to it. The material is not metal, not ceramic, not polymer, not crystal. It simply is, running in a perfect line around the equator of a world that has no other reason to be remembered.
